name: SKU Generator
description: Build a structured SKU from a category code, product name, and variant — with an optional random suffix for uniqueness.

faq.question: How is the SKU built?
faq.answer: Each field you fill in (category code, product name, variant) is uppercased, stripped of anything that isn't a letter or number, and truncated to a reasonable length, then joined with your chosen separator. An optional random numeric suffix at the end helps keep otherwise-identical SKUs unique.

faq.question: Is the random suffix actually unique?
faq.answer: It's drawn from your browser's cryptographically secure random number generator, so a 4-digit suffix has a 1-in-10,000 chance of colliding with another SKU generated the same way — fine for most small catalogs, but for guaranteed uniqueness at scale you'll still want to check against your actual product database.

faq.question: Does this follow a specific SKU standard?
faq.answer: No — there's no universal SKU standard; every retailer defines their own format. This tool gives you a consistent, structured pattern to start from, which you can adapt to match your own conventions.
